name: Pneumos DIY teeth whitening

card.summary: A home teeth-whitening method popularised on looksmax.org by a user known as pneumo, using dental-grade high-concentration peroxide to brighten teeth for a whiter smile.
card.note: High-concentration peroxide can burn gums and damage tissue; EU retail limit is 0.1% and professional use is capped at 6%.

quick.overview:
The pneumos method is a do-it-yourself take on in-office whitening, described in a looksmax.org guide titled around whitening teeth better than a dentist. Its aim is visibly whiter teeth, which community members say lifts overall facial attractiveness and confidence.

Users who followed it posted before-and-after pictures and positive reports, while others on the forum asked whether it was too risky. No clinical study has tested the home protocol itself.
quick.how: Forum posts describe gathering dental-style supplies such as a gum barrier gel, cheek retractors, a high-percentage peroxide gel and a curing light, protecting the gums and applying the gel to the teeth, as an at-home copy of professional whitening. The wiki does not reproduce the steps.
quick.risks: Peroxide at 10% or higher can damage tissue, and chemical burns happen when strong agent reaches unprotected gums. Enamel changes and sensitivity are documented with bleaching. In the EU, retail whitening is limited to 0.1% peroxide and up to 6% under a dental professional.

lead: The pneumos method is a do-it-yourself teeth-whitening procedure shared on looksmax.org by a user called pneumo. The original guide claimed to whiten teeth better than a dentist, and later threads by other users reported attempts [1][2]. Followers say whiter teeth improve smile aesthetics and confidence.

The approach mimics a professional in-office power-bleaching session using supplies ordered by the user, including gum-protection gel, retractors, a high-concentration peroxide gel and a dental curing light [1]. One reporter said it took four attempts to place the gum barrier correctly [1].
Some forum users asked others about their experience before trying, noting that it sounds risky [2]. Dental references describe the hazards of strong peroxide products [3].

chain: High-strength peroxide gel applied to teeth
angle.text: Forum users use the method to brighten tooth shade at home, with before-and-after photos posted as evidence. The goal is a whiter smile at lower cost than a dental visit.

paras: A user reported trying pneumo's guide after finding it on the forum, saying his teeth were never especially yellow but he wanted to maximise every metric of appearance [1]. His posted before-and-after photos drew supportive replies [1]. Another user said he had found a source for high-concentration peroxide and wanted others' results before trying, noting that others consider the method pretty risky and that high-percentage strips had given a modest brightness increase and improved his confidence [2].

In-office gels typically deliver roughly 3% to 16% hydrogen peroxide equivalent, with power-bleaching gels reaching 25% to 38% hydrogen peroxide under professional use [3]. Peroxide at 10% or higher can damage tissue, and chemical burns occur when strong agent contacts unprotected gums; in-office procedures paint a protective layer on the gums for this reason [3]. Bleaching can temporarily demineralise enamel and increase roughness [3]. In the EU, retail products are limited to 0.1% hydrogen peroxide and up to 6% under a dental professional, and only dental professionals may administer bleaching agents [3]. Evidence on light activation is mixed [3].
No studies found on the pneumos home protocol. Dental bleaching in general has been studied extensively under professional conditions [3].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the method is presented both as a cost-saving route to a whiter smile and as a risky one, with members sharing results and asking about safety [1][2].

claims.claim: Home use of strong peroxide whitens teeth "better than a dentist"
claims.believers: Posters share before-and-after images and say results were visible after trying the guide [1].
claims.experts: Dental sources say strong peroxide can burn unprotected gums, and professionals use protective barriers and regulated concentrations [3].

claims.claim: Whiter teeth give a mental and social benefit
claims.believers: One poster says white teeth help confidence more than physically, and that even modest strip results boosted his confidence [2].
claims.experts: No published study is cited here on this specific community claim.
